question: Why are subspaces important in machine learning?
direct_answer: They capture lower-dimensional structure inside larger feature spaces.
expanded_answer: A subspace is a subset that is itself a vector space, often geometrically a line or plane through the origin. In ML, data may lie near a lower-dimensional subspace even when embedded in a high-dimensional space. This is one reason techniques like PCA and other dimensionality-reduction methods can work well.
key_points: A subspace is closed under vector operations
Often looks like a line or plane through the origin
Explains low-dimensional structure in high-dimensional data
common_wrong_ideas: Any cluster of points is a subspace
A subspace can be shifted away from the origin and still be a vector space
A subspace must use fewer coordinates
